# @zakkster/lite-gc-profiler v1.15.1

Zero-dependency GC and heap profiler that makes the zero-GC claim
falsifiable. Precise perf_hooks GC entries in node, heap-drop heuristic
in Chrome, accurate opt-in measureUserAgentSpecificMemory (`uasm`)
also in Chrome under cross-origin isolation, frame-anomaly fallback
elsewhere. Three-state gate verdicts (pass/fail/inconclusive), phases,
nesting regions, differential and rep-aware gating, per-op primitives
(measureOps/assertOps/compareOps) for hot-path gating, baselines with
fingerprinting, CLI with partial-report handling for hard exits,
node:test helper, explain mode via node:inspector heap sampling.
Single-file browser surface; node-only subpaths for register/
test-helpers/explain and the lite-gc-gate CLI.

Framework integration (Vue/React/Angular): there is nothing
framework-specific to install -- gate a reactive tick (an effect re-run,
a render, a change-detection cycle) with measureAllocs/assertAllocs under
--expose-gc (Vitest: execArgv ['--expose-gc']). See COOKBOOK recipes
23-25 and the runnable, zero-dependency examples/ directory.

## Entry points

- `@zakkster/lite-gc-profiler` (browser-safe, main): `GcProfiler`,
  `checkNoGc`, `assertNoGc`, `compareGc`, `assertCompare`,
  `aggregateGc`, `gateReps`, `assertReps`,
  `measureOps`, `checkOps`, `assertOps`,
  `compareOps`, `assertCompareOps`,
  `measureAllocs`, `checkAllocs`, `assertAllocs`,
  `measureFrames`, `checkFrames`, `assertFrames`,
  `compareFrames`, `assertCompareFrames`,
  `measureOpsAsync`, `checkOpsAsync`, `assertOpsAsync`,
  `compareOpsAsync`, `assertCompareOpsAsync`,
  `aggregateWorkerReports`, `checkAggregateReport`, `assertAggregateReport`,
  `aggregateFrameReports`, `checkAggregateFramesReport`, `assertAggregateFramesReport`,
  `captureFingerprint`,
  `createBaseline`, `checkAgainstBaseline`, `assertAgainstBaseline`,
  `ratchetBaseline`,
  `formatConsole`, `formatJson`, `formatMarkdown`,
  `formatGithubAnnotations`, `GcBudgetError`, `GcInconclusiveError`,
  `watchPool`, `assertNoEscapes`, `GcPoolEscapeError`,
  `GC_DEFAULT_RULES`, `GC_DEFAULT_DIFFERENTIAL_RULES`,
  `REP_POLICY_DEFAULTS`, `VERDICT_MATRIX`, `VERSION`,
  `GC_MINOR`/`GC_MAJOR`/`GC_INCREMENTAL`/`GC_WEAKCB`.
- `@zakkster/lite-gc-profiler/register` (node): auto-attach preload.
- `@zakkster/lite-gc-profiler/test-helpers` (node): `withGcGate`,
  `measureGc`.
- `@zakkster/lite-gc-profiler/explain` (node + browser-safe formatters):
  `startExplainSampling`, `formatExplainConsole` (node-only heap sampler);
  `explainReport`, `explainDiff`, `gateBadge` (v1.6.0 evidence lane:
  pure gate-report formatters; browser-safe; no measurement, no
  observer, no perturbation).
- `bin/lite-gc-gate` (CLI).

## Key semantics

- Three-state verdict never silently green on unverifiable rules.
- Rule keys are lane-scoped (v1.15.1). `checkNoGc` accepts ONLY the six rules it
  evaluates (`maxMajor`, `maxMinor`, `maxPauseMs`, `maxTotalMs`, `maxAllocRate`,
  `maxArrayBuffersGrowth`); a summary carries no per-op/per-frame metric, so a
  key that belongs to another lane -- `maxBytesPerOp` (checkOps), `maxBytesPerCall`
  (checkAllocs), `maxBytesPerFrame`/`maxDroppedFrames` (checkFrames), ... -- is
  REJECTED with a `TypeError` naming the owning lane, not accepted-and-dropped.
  Three outcomes: ungated -> wrong-lane -> typo. Before v1.15.1 those ten keys
  passed validation and were silently ignored, a fail-open on the primary lane
  (GC-02). The rejection recurses through `phases` and `perRegion`.
- Never-observed profiler is inconclusive, not green (v1.15.0). `summary.observed`
  is false iff the profiler never `start()`ed AND never took synthetic data
  (record/sampleHeap/sampleUasm/markFrame/phase/enter). `checkNoGc` routes
  `observed:false` to `inconclusive` (reason `not_observed`) -- a summary nobody
  watched cannot pass. Only an explicit false triggers this; a hand-built/legacy
  summary (observed undefined) is unaffected.
- Formatters and canary assert fail-closed (v1.15.0). The four `format*` gate
  formatters throw a named `TypeError` on a non-report (no string `verdict`) --
  `formatJson` no longer envelopes engine internals as a valid `lite-gc-report/1`,
  `formatGithubAnnotations` no longer emits "gate passed" for a verdict-less
  document. `assertNoEscapes` throws `TypeError` on a non-report (no `escapes`
  array) but still never throws on a valid EMPTY report (absence stays advisory).
  `ratchetBaseline` returns `baseline:null` on `invalid_baseline` rather than
  echoing the mis-passed argument back under the baseline key.
- Gates fail CLOSED (v1.5.1, extended v1.5.2). An unknown rule key throws
  `TypeError` rather than matching nothing; a non-finite or non-numeric
  threshold throws `RangeError` on the ops/frames lanes and yields
  `inconclusive` on the `checkNoGc` lane; a non-finite metric yields
  `inconclusive`, never `pass`. Do not pass rule keys a lane does not
  implement. Rule thresholds are read exactly once, so a getter cannot
  return one value to validation and another to the comparison.
- `uasm` is quantized and the quantum is not contractual (v1.9.0). Each
  window derives its own floor -- `summary.uasm.granularityBytes`, the
  smallest non-zero step between consecutive readings, or `null` when no
  step occurred (null means NOT MEASURED; never render or compare it as
  0). `summary.uasm.belowGranularity` is true when the window's net
  displacement sits inside one quantum or no floor was measured at all;
  `maxAllocRate` on `source: 'uasm'` then routes to `inconclusive` with
  `reason: 'uasm_below_granularity'` -- never pass, never fail. Same on
  `maxExtraAllocRate` (a delta is only as resolvable as its worse side)
  and on `gateReps` (ANY blind rep makes the set unresolvable).
  `growthRate` stays the RAW net/time figure and is not zeroed under the
  flag: the rate is the measurement, the flag is whether it resolves.
- `maxArrayBuffersGrowth` (v1.10.0) gates net growth of ArrayBuffer backing
  stores, which live OUTSIDE the V8 heap and are invisible to `maxAllocRate`
  (measured blind spot: 152x). Node/`source:'gc'` only. Requires
  `stabilize:'deep'` on measureOps, or `gc.forceSettle()` before each sample
  on the manual path; otherwise `summary.arrayBuffers.settled` is false and
  the rule is inconclusive. There is NO `maxExternalGrowth` -- passing it
  throws; `summary.external` is diagnostic only because it reconciles lazily.
- `summary.gc.foreignForced` (v1.10.0, node only) counts forced collections
  the library did NOT cause. Non-zero means something else collected inside
  the measured window and the numbers are polluted. Diagnostic; not gated.
- Unknown rule keys throw on EVERY lane including `checkNoGc` as of v1.10.0
  (before that, `checkNoGc` silently ignored them and returned `pass`).
- Triage for the third verdict lives in `INCONCLUSIVE.md` (shipped).
  Reason codes: `source_mismatch`, `mixed_sources`, `fingerprint_mismatch`,
  `no_comparable_metrics`, `invalid_baseline`, `partial_report`,
  `uasm_below_granularity`, `not_observed`. `GcInconclusiveError.message` names the cause
  and one next step; do not resolve an unexpected `inconclusive` by
  setting `allowInconclusive` -- that is the escape hatch, not the fix.
- One measurement at a time. Overlapping/nested `measureOps`,
  `measureFrames` or `measureOpsAsync` throws/rejects "already in
  flight" -- all lanes share one heap. Measure sequentially. The guard
  releases when a run settles; a run that NEVER settles (a scheduler
  that never fires, a promise that never resolves) holds it for the life
  of the process by design -- releasing on a timeout would resume the
  cross-contamination the guard prevents.
- `opts.capacity` must be a positive integer <= 2**24 (MAX_RING_CAPACITY)
  in every lane, and the GcProfiler constructor enforces the same ceiling
  (v1.5.2). Past it: RangeError. Before the ceiling, capacities above
  2**30 hung the process (32-bit shift wrap in pow2) and large ones below
  it silently allocated GB-scale rings.
- The overlapping-measurement guard is per module instance. Two copies
  of Gc.js (source + bundled) each keep their own counter and cannot see
  each other's in-flight runs. Import the profiler once.
- `record()` requires a finite durationMs >= 0 and a finite startTime
  when given; both throw RangeError otherwise (v1.5.2).
- start() and reset() are hard cutoffs (v1.5.2): 'gc' entries whose
  startTime precedes them are dropped even when node delivers the queued
  backlog of an earlier sync workload later in the same turn. A profiler
  never inherits GC history it did not observe; the synthetic record()
  API is exempt.
- Phases (linear, no nesting), regions (nested, LIFO enter/exit).
- Attribution is firing-site, not allocator. Explain mode answers the
  allocator question separately via node:inspector heap sampling.
- Rep policy defaults: majors/minors -> all-clean, pauses/rates ->
  best-clean. Override per rule.
- Baseline regression semantic: current.median > baseline.max. Both
  comparands must be finite; a metric whose baseline `max` is NaN/null/
  non-numeric reports `checked: false` (v1.5.2). A baseline with no
  comparable metrics at all -> `inconclusive` with
  `reason: 'no_comparable_metrics'`, never `pass`.
- Fingerprint mismatch -> inconclusive (D6).
- ratchetBaseline (G28, v1.12.0): tighten a committed baseline toward a
  PASSING run. Returns { baseline, ratcheted, changed, reason? }; every
  metric is the element-wise min of old and current, so a floor only ever
  moves DOWN. A metric absent or non-finite in the current aggregate is
  carried forward unchanged (never min against a hole). Fingerprint-guarded
  like checkAgainstBaseline. Pure min -> misuse can only fail to tighten,
  never enshrine a regression. Distinct from --update-baseline, which
  overwrites in either direction. It closes the static-floor blind spot: a
  baseline frozen at major=8 passes a regression 3->7; a ratcheted floor at
  3 catches it.
- CLI --ratchet (v1.12.0): on `lite-gc-gate run ... --baseline b.json
  --ratchet`, capture -> checkAgainstBaseline -> on pass rewrite b.json
  tighter (prints what moved), on fail/inconclusive leave it byte-identical
  and exit non-zero. Requires --baseline; mutually exclusive with
  --update-baseline.
- `summary.phases`/`summary.byRegion` define keys via defineProperty
  (v1.5.2), so a phase named `__proto__` is a real key. Prototype and
  shape are unchanged; no assertion style change is needed.
- `sampleHeap()` ignores non-finite readings rather than letting them
  poison subsequent allocation accounting (v1.5.2).
- CLI exit codes: 0 pass, 1 fail, 2 inconclusive, 3 infrastructure error.

## Zero-alloc guarantees

Hot-path methods (`record`, `sampleHeap`, `markFrame`, `phase`, `enter`,
`exit`) allocate nothing after the intern tables settle. Observer
callback increments one integer per batch beyond delivering entries.
Self-noise on old hardware: 0 majors, 2-4 minors, ~0.5 ms longest pause,
250-770 KB heap growth per 500ms noop window (mostly V8, not the
profiler).

`measureAllocs` (v1.11.0) turns this into an assertion you can run on
your OWN hot path: it measures per-call RETAINED bytes (allocation
surviving a forced collection) via a min-over-batches estimator, so
`maxBytesPerCall: 0` is the literal zero-retention claim. Requires
`--expose-gc`; rejects async fns (use `measureOpsAsync`); an unsettled
or non-finite run is inconclusive, never a false pass. Distinct from
`measureOps`, which reports an allocation RATE (`maxBytesPerOp`) and
sees transient garbage that `measureAllocs` settles away.

Allocation attribution (G27, v1.13.0): `measureAllocs(fn, { attribute:
true })` runs node:inspector's HeapProfiler SAMPLING profiler over the
batch loop and attaches `result.attribution` = { available, reason?,
totalSampledBytes, nativeBytes, sites: [{ function, url, line, column,
selfBytes, selfPct }] }, heaviest first (topSites default 5). checkAllocs
appends the top site to a failure reason. LOAD-BEARING: attribution NEVER
gates -- sampling is probabilistic, the top site is a hint, bytesPerCall
gates exactly as before and attribution's absence is benign (the inverse
of every other lane's fail-closed rule). Node-only; degrades to
{ available: false, reason: 'no_inspector' | 'connect_failed' |
'start_failed' | 'stop_failed' } elsewhere, never throws. One inspector
session per call, born+buried inside the measurement guard (never pooled),
torn down even if the workload throws. Native/internal/library frames are
filtered to a separate nativeBytes bucket. Without `attribute`, inspector
is never touched and attribution is null.

Pool-escape canary (watchPool, v1.14.0): a DETECTOR for the INVERSE of a
leak -- a pooled object that should live DIES (escaped the pool's
bookkeeping, lost its last ref, got collected). `watchPool({ label })`
returns a handle: register(obj, slotId) on checkout, release(obj, slotId)
on checkin, `await settle({ cycles, gap })` to drive gc + macrotask yield
and collect the report { available, reason?, escapes:[{slot}], escapeCount,
settled, watched, released, label, note }, then dispose(). assertNoEscapes
throws GcPoolEscapeError iff escapes.length > 0. FOUR LAWS, each forced by
the measured fact that FinalizationRegistry callbacks fire only after a
collection AND a macrotask (never synchronously with gc()): (1) async by
construction, no sync form; (2) escapes are asserted but ABSENCE IS NOT --
an empty escapes list is "none seen in N cycles", never "none exist", so
there is no clean/pass verdict and assertNoEscapes never throws on empty
(the inverse of measureAllocs's maxBytesPerCall:0 negative gate); (3)
Node + modern-engine only, degrades to { available:false, reason:
'no_registry' | 'no_gc' }, never throws for lack of the mechanism; (4) the
registry holds the slot id as held value and the object only as a weak
target -- holding the object would pin every slot and report zero escapes
by construction. Does NOT compose with stabilize:'deep' (sync anchor vs
async finalizer). A released-then-collected slot is NOT an escape.
